title: Compact requirements document
description: Optional editor aid for a requirements.yaml in the requirements-yaml format. Structural only — it enforces no grammar and gates nothing. Authoring and review rules live in the requirements-yaml skill (SKILL.md).
markdownDescription: Compact requirements. One line each: `<ID>: <capability>; so that <value>; verified when <observable proof>.` Grouped into `functional` (area → `As a <role>, I can:` → ID), `non_functional` (quality → ID), optional `deferred`, an optional `docs` map (filename → what it is and when to read it), and project domain sections. Full rules: the **requirements-yaml** skill.

goals.description: Optional list of project goals — the vision the requirements serve. Free one-line statements, not requirements: no IDs, no clauses. Kept first by convention.

non_goals.description: Optional list of non-goals — boundaries the project deliberately will not cross. Distinct from `deferred` (merely not-yet); a non-goal is not-ever. Free one-line statements, not requirements.

docs.description: Optional map of supporting documents. Each key is a document filename (a repo-relative path or a URL); each value describes what the document is and when it should be read.

functional.description: Functional requirements grouped by system area, then (recommended) by story role.

non_functional.description: Non-functional requirements grouped by quality attribute.

deferred.description: Explicitly deferred / future requirements grouped by area.

snakeCaseKey.description: A lower snake_case grouping key such as `accounts`, `data_policy`, or `openness_and_governance`.

statement.description: A free one-line goal or non-goal statement: a distilled direction or boundary, not a requirement — no ID, no `so that`/`verified when`. Quote it when it starts with `[?]` or another YAML indicator.

roleKey.description: A role heading: `As a <role>, I can`, so requirement lines can start with the capability verb.

requirementId.description: A stable requirement ID: uppercase area prefix plus a zero-padded number.

deferredRequirementId.description: A stable future-scope ID: the normal ID prefixed with `[deferred] `.

requirementText.description: One requirement line. Recommended: `<capability>; so that <value>; verified when <observable proof>.` Under a role heading, start with the verb. Quote only if a clause contains `: ` or the value starts with a YAML indicator.

docPath.description: A supporting document's filename: a repo-relative path (e.g. `docs/glossary.md`) or a URL.

docDescription.description: What the document is and, importantly, when it should be read — e.g. `the ubiquitous language — read before naming anything in a requirement`.

requirementMap.description: A map of requirement IDs to one-line requirement text.

deferredRequirementMap.description: A map of deferred requirement IDs to one-line requirement text. Used only under `deferred`.

functionalArea.description: A system-area section: group by role heading (`As a <role>, I can`) whose value is a requirement map, or put a requirement map directly if roles are not used.

domainSection.description: A project-specific top-level section: snake_case subgroups whose values are requirement maps, like `non_functional`.
